Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Class P2pServer

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.P2pServer
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class P2pServer extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The inbound half of a P2P node: a ServerSocket plus a daemon accept loop. Each accepted socket is handed to a P2pServer.ChannelAcceptor on its own daemon thread, so a slow or hostile inbound handshake can never stall the loop (and one connection cannot deny service to the next). Established channels are surfaced to an onConnected sink; failures to an onError sink.

This class is deliberately dumb about P2P semantics: it knows nothing about identities, handshakes or peers. The P2pNode supplies the acceptor that runs the NoiseXXHandshake and adopts the resulting SecureChannel, which keeps the socket plumbing independently testable. The server binds to the wildcard address so LAN peers can reach it; port 0 selects an ephemeral port (read it back with getPort()).

All threads are daemons, so a running server never pins the JVM open. The server is headless-safe: it touches no AWT/Swing class.

    • P2pServer

      public P2pServer(int port, P2pServer.ChannelAcceptor acceptor, Consumer<SecureChannel> onConnected, Consumer<String> onError) throws IOException
      Binds and starts accepting immediately.
      Parameters:
      port - the TCP port to listen on (0 for an ephemeral port)
      acceptor - turns each accepted socket into a channel (never null)
      onConnected - receives each established channel (may be null)
      onError - receives human-readable failure notes (may be null)
      Throws:
      IOException - if the port cannot be bound
